reading.h2: The Life of Saint Tekle Haimanot

reading.p: Saint Tekle Haimanot is honored as the six-winged pillar of faith. His name means "Plant of Faith," and his Gädlä (life story) elaborates this as "Plant of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit." He was a monk, hermit, missionary, and the founder of Debre Libanos Monastery in Shewa.

He was born in Zorare (Bulga, Shewa) to the priest Tsega Ze'ab, whose name means "Grace of God," and to Egzi'e Haraya, whose name means "Choice of God" and who was also called Sarah. His feast day is August 30 (Gregorian) or Nehase 24 (Ethiopian), and his veneration is official in Rome and in Egypt (the Coptic Church). In iconography he is depicted with six wings, signifying Seraphic grace, and standing on one leg, a sign of unceasing, sacrificial prayer.

reading.h2: The State of Ethiopia in the 13th Century

reading.p: Saint Tekle Haimanot lived in Ethiopia's central and southern provinces, such as Shewa, where he was born. It was a period of political instability following the Zagwe Dynasty. Spiritually, Christianity remained strong in the North but had weakened in the South.

list: Syncretism: many people mixed Christian beliefs with local pagan rituals and spirit worship.
Isolation: priests were few, and monastic centers of learning were far away.
A need for re-evangelization from within.

reading.h2: Childhood: A Child of Prophecy and Early Grace

reading.p: His father was the priest Tsega Ze'ab ("Grace of God") and his mother was Egzi'e Haraya ("Choice of God," also known as Sarah). They were a righteous, wealthy, and devout couple who were barren and childless for many years. They prayed constantly, fasted, and gave alms, pledging their firstborn child to the service of God.
Then the Archangel Michael appeared to them, announcing that they would bear a son who would "renew the faith of Ethiopia" and be a light to the nation.

While he was a young deacon, the Archangel Michael appeared to him in the forest and gave him a direct and specific command. He was to renounce the world entirely, to give up the marriage his parents had arranged for him, and to dedicate his whole life to saving souls and preaching the Gospel. It was at this moment that the angel gave him his new, prophetic name: Tekle Haimanot, "Plant of Faith."

Following this call, the Archangel directed him to go to the Coptic Bishop, Abuna Kirollos (Cyril) of Alexandria, who was visiting the region. Recognizing the divine grace in him, the bishop ordained him as a priest.

reading.h3: The Two Streams of Monastic Training

list: Lake Hayq (Istefanos Monastery): he studied under Abba Iyasus Mo'a, learning the communal (cenobitic) life, theology, and chant.
Debre Damo: he traveled to the legendary clifftop monastery of Abba Aragawi to learn the severe, solitary (hermit) life of asceticism.

reading.h2: The Miracle of the Six Wings

reading.p: After nine years at Debre Damo, an angel commanded him to descend and begin his mission to the South. The monks began to lower him by rope from the sheer cliff, which was the only way down. Halfway down, the rope snapped; his Gädlä says that Satan, enraged at his obedience, cut the rope. As he fell, six brilliant wings burst from his back, and he flew safely to the ground.

This was his "ordination by heaven," the divine seal of approval that confirmed his apostolic mission and identified him with the Seraphim. The six wings are a symbol of divine grace and angelic zeal, each wing representing Faith, Hope, Charity, Obedience, Purity, and Humility.

Guided by the Holy Spirit, Saint Tekle Haimanot entered the pagan kingdom of Damot, where he first made contact with the Prince, the chief noble and heir. The saint demonstrated the power of Christ by casting out a demon and healing the Prince from a grave affliction, which led to the Prince's immediate conversion and baptism.

The King, Motolomi, was furious that his heir and court had converted, seeing it as the collapse of his religious and political authority, which relied on the worship of a great serpent idol called zedo. Motolomi escalated the conflict and sent an army to kill both the saint and the converted Prince. But the soldiers' spears, thrown at the saint, stopped in mid-air. When Motolomi threw his own spear, it reversed direction and killed his horse, a symbol of his earthly power, while mercifully sparing his life.

Then the saint cursed the serpent idol, which died, and prayed, causing rain to fall immediately during the severe drought. Humbled by these acts of judgment and mercy, King Motolomi, the Prince, and the entire populace repented, were baptized, and consecrated their land to Christ.

After his mission, he founded the monastery of Debre Libanos ("Mount of Lebanon") in Shewa. This monastery grew to become the single most important spiritual center in all of Ethiopia. He established the office of the Ichege, the Abbot of Debre Libanos.

The Ichege became the highest-ranking native-born Church official in Ethiopia, second only to the Coptic Abuna. This gave the Ethiopian Church administrative stability and a unified, internal leadership for the first time, and Debre Libanos became the "mother monastery" for hundreds of other monasteries across the nation.

reading.h2: Seven Years on One Leg: The Triumph of Spirit Over Flesh

reading.p: In his old age, he devoted himself to unceasing prayer, vowing to stand for the rest of his life. He stood in prayer day and night, without sitting or lying down, for seven years. From this unceasing vigil, his leg decayed from fatigue and broke off, yet he continued his prayer, standing on the one remaining leg for the rest of his life.
This is the ultimate symbol of endurance, of sacrificing his body as a "living sacrifice" (Romans 12:1).

reading.h2: Summary: The Apostle, the Founder, the Pillar

reading.p: Saint Tekle Haimanot is important to the Orthodox Church because he is a model of both apostolic mission, signified by the six wings, and ascetic devotion, signified by the one leg. He connects the scholarly life of Hayq with the ascetic life of Damo and with the official Church of Alexandria.

He is a special saint for Ethiopia in three ways: as the Apostle of the South, he re-Christianized half the nation; as the Great Unifier, he founded Debre Libanos and the office of the Ichege, giving the Ethiopian Church its own national leadership; and as the National Icon, he is the ultimate model of Ethiopian piety, endurance, and sacrificial faith.
His final lesson is that true faith is a "plant": it must be nurtured through formation, spread through mission, and rooted in total sacrifice through endurance. He is an embodiment of theosis.

studyGuide.overview: Saint Tekle Haimanot ("Plant of Faith") was a 13th-century Ethiopian monk, hermit, and missionary who re-evangelized the weakened and syncretistic South, founded Debre Libanos Monastery, and established the office of the Ichege. He is venerated with six wings, symbolizing his apostolic mission, and standing on one leg, symbolizing his unceasing, sacrificial prayer.
keyPoints: His name means 'Plant of Faith,' elaborated as 'Plant of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.'
He was a child of prophecy; the Archangel Michael announced his birth and later called him to renounce the world.
He was ordained priest by the Coptic Bishop Abuna Kirollos (Cyril) of Alexandria and trained at Lake Hayq and Debre Damo.
The miracle of the six wings was his 'ordination by heaven,' confirming his apostolic mission; each wing represents Faith, Hope, Charity, Obedience, Purity, and Humility.
He evangelized the pagan kingdom of Damot, converting King Motolomi and the people through miracles of judgment and mercy.
He founded Debre Libanos (c. 1284) and established the Ichege, giving the Ethiopian Church its own native leadership.
He stood in prayer for seven years until his leg broke off, embodying endurance and theosis.
reviewQuestions: What does the name Tekle Haimanot mean, and how does his Gädlä expand it?
What was the spiritual condition of southern Ethiopia in the 13th century, and why was re-evangelization needed?
How did the miracle of the six wings come about, and what does it signify?
How did Saint Tekle Haimanot bring King Motolomi and the kingdom of Damot to Christ?
What was the office of the Ichege, and why was it so important for the Ethiopian Church?
How does his seven years of standing prayer illustrate sacrifice and theosis?

checks: Veneration of the monastic saint Tekle Haimanot, including his feast (Nehase 24) and iconography, is proper to the Ethiopian Tewahedo tradition.
His ordination by the Coptic Bishop of Alexandria and the relationship of the Ichege to the Coptic Abuna correctly reflect the historic communion of the Oriental Orthodox (non-Chalcedonian) Churches.
The role of the Archangel Michael and the saint's miracles are presented as found in his Gädlä; the source's own attribution ('His Gädlä says') is preserved rather than asserted independently.
The closing reference to theosis (becoming like God by grace) aligns with Orthodox teaching and was not embellished.
No content was added beyond the source, and nothing conflicts with the Miaphysite confession or the first three Ecumenical Councils.
